summary: RFCs 4328 and 7139 give RSVP-TE signaling extensions for controlling Optical Transport Network features, but they do not cover the additional ODU containers defined in G.Sup43. This informational document adds the signaling needed for those extra signal types.

plainLanguage.summary: Optical networks carry data in standard-sized containers. A few newer container sizes were missing from the setup instructions, so this adds them.

questions: what signal types does rsvp-te support for otn
subtitle: Signaling extensions for optical transport network containers

tldr.problem: The previous RSVP-TE specifications for controlling optical transport networks did not include signal types for three newer container formats (ODU1e, ODU3e1, and ODU3e2) defined for transporting high-speed Ethernet signals.
tldr.mechanism: This document defines and registers the missing signal types with their corresponding numerical values, allowing RSVP-TE to signal these additional Optical channel Data Unit containers.
tldr.outcome: Network operators can now use RSVP-TE to control and manage the newer ODU container types in their optical transport networks.

today: RFC 7963 is an Informational RFC that has not been obsoleted. It provides the IANA registrations needed for RSVP-TE to work with these additional ODU container types in optical networks.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Optical Transport Networks (OTN) use standardized containers called Optical channel Data Units (ODUs) to carry different types of signals. These containers come in different sizes to handle various data rates.

RFC 7139 describes how to use RSVP-TE (Resource ReserVation Protocol with Traffic Engineering) to signal and control OTN features. However, it only covers the containers defined in ITU-T G.709-v3. Three additional container types defined in ITU-T G.Sup43 were missing from those specifications: ODU1e, ODU3e1, and ODU3e2, which carry 10 Gbps and 40 Gbps Ethernet signals.
sections.plainLanguage: The instructions for telling the network about different sized containers did not include the new sizes, so this document adds them.

sections.title: The Missing Signal Types
sections.content:
RFC 7139 defines a Signal Type field in RSVP-TE traffic parameters. This document registers three new signal types to represent the additional ODU containers: ODU1e (value 23) for 10 Gbps Ethernet, ODU3e1 (value 26) for 40 Gbps Ethernet, and ODU3e2 (value 27), also for 40 Gbps Ethernet.

These containers are non-standard data-plane formats not formally defined by ITU-T. They represent intra-domain approaches some optical networks use to transport high-speed Ethernet signals. While they solve practical problems, they do not guarantee interoperability across different vendors' equipment.
sections.plainLanguage: Three new container types now have official numbers so the network knows what they are.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: This document only adds signal type definitions. It does not introduce any new security issues beyond those already identified in RFC 7139, which already covers RSVP-TE security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: These changes are just adding names to existing things, so there are no new safety concerns.
